name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Doubly Committed Ventricular Septal Defect
aliases: Double outlet right ventricle with subarterial VSD

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of both great arteries arising predominantly from the right ventricle confirmed by imaging
Identification of a ventricular septal defect located beneath both the aortic and pulmonary valves
Clinical features consistent with cyanotic congenital heart disease such as central cyanosis and heart murmur

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of both great arteries arising from the right ventricle with a doubly committed ventricular septal defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac catheterization or MRI may be used to further delineate anatomy if echocardiography is inconclusive.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border
pathognomonic.notes: Due to turbulent flow across the ventricular septal defect and outflow tracts
searchTerms: heart murmur heard at upper left chest
systolic murmur at left upper sternum
ejection murmur at left upper chest

common.notes: Shortness of breath during physical activity
Poor weight gain and growth in infants
Early tiredness during feeding due to decreased cardiac output

occasional.notes: Swelling of lower limbs due to right heart failure
Enlarged liver secondary to congestive heart failure
Transient loss of consciousness due to decreased cerebral perfusion
Abnormal heart rhythms detected on ECG

rare.notes: Embolic events secondary to right-to-left shunting
searchTerms: stroke from embolism crossing heart defect
brain infarct due to embolus crossing circulation

rare.notes: Infection of the heart valves or endocardium
Elevated pressure in pulmonary arteries secondary to shunting

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary erythrocytosis
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from right ventricle and doubly committed VSD
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Overriding aorta rather than both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Pulmonary stenosis with right ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
No ventricular septal defect or non-committed VSD
Parallel rather than side-by-side great arteries

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomy and diagnosis. Heart. 2014;100(5):394-400.
Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th ed. Wiley-Blackwell; 2013.
